newsitem.title: USA: NY Governor would limit SOx allowance trading.
newsitem.headline: NY Governor would limit SOx allowance trading.

text.p: New York Governor George Pataki Tuesday proposed legislation seeking licensing and disclosure of sulfur dioxide trading, the executive office said in a statement.

Citing Long Island Lighting Co allowance sales to Midwest companies, he said "this legilation will build in strong protections by prohibiting the sale of sulfur dioxide allowances to out-of-state sources whose emissions would increase acid rain damage within our borders."

For the first time, the statement said, the proposal wouldrequire the Department of State to license brokers who buy and sell these allowances, explaining this would open the process to full public disclosure.

Under the legislation, any New York State source interested in selling sulfur dioxide allowances outside the state would be required to offer them first to the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority.
Also, any entity which has received a state grant, loan, tax credit or other approval from a state agency or authority would be prohibited from selling allowances to entities outside the state.
